turns.question: i am an employee of a board of park commissioners, how is my pension calculated?
turns.answer:
Your pension is calculated under **Article 12**, which your record identifies as your applicable article. Article 12 defines service to include covered employment, certain approved leave, credited military service, and certain disability periods. [40 ILCS 5/12-109]

For a retirement on or after December 31, 2003, Section 12-133 provides a retirement annuity of **2.40% for each year of service** multiplied by your **highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within your last 10 years of service**. Service of less than a full year is prorated. The annuity is generally limited to **80%** of that salary average. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

Because you are under age 60, the annuity is generally reduced by **¼ of 1% for each month or fraction of a month** that your age is below 60. That reduction does not apply to an employee retiring at age 50 or over with at least 30 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

Section 12-130 also applies to an employee who withdraws before age 60 with at least 10 years of service and allows the retirement annuity to begin after withdrawal or attainment of age 50, whichever is later. It does not provide the fixed-benefit formula; Section 12-133 provides that formula. [40 ILCS 5/12-130]

Section 12-131 provides the accumulation-based calculation for retirement at age 60 or over. It is not the provision for a retirement before age 60. [40 ILCS 5/12-131] Section 12-128 describes the retirement annuity as consisting of a service annuity and, where applicable, a prior service annuity. [40 ILCS 5/12-128]

An exact pension figure cannot be worked out without your age at withdrawal and your highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within your last 10 years of service. Your record shows **21.5 years of service**. The statute also requires the fund to apply its service and salary rules, including the definition of “highest salary.” [40 ILCS 5/12-108]

I'm going by your record, which places you in Article 12 — tell me if that's not right.

turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas. The main formula for a qualifying employee with at least 20 years of service is **2.40% for each year of service**, based on the highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years of service. The maximum is **80% of that salary basis**. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The section also provides an early-retirement reduction of **0.25% for each full month or fractional part of a month** that the annuity begins before age 60. Certain age-and-service combinations are exempt from that reduction. The section gives additional formulas, including an election for some employees with at least 10 years of service whose annuity begins no earlier than age 60. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

Your **21.5 years of service** must be determined under the minimum-annuity service-credit rules. Those rules count specified employment, paid leave, certain disability periods, and certain labor-organization leaves; service during **6 or more months** in a year counts as a year, while service of less than 6 months and at least 1 month counts as a half year. [40 ILCS 5/11-216]
